clue.text: Outlying part of Eden — or Hampstead?

definitions.text: Outlying part of Eden — or Hampstead?

parts.words: Outlying part of Eden — or Hampstead?
parts.note: the fringe of the biblical paradise is jokingly pictured as its residential outskirts, and Hampstead in north London has a famous planned estate of that kind

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about where Paradise's outskirts lie, comparing them to a leafy London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Eden was a garden, so its outlying part would be the garden's suburb; Hampstead Garden Suburb is a real planned residential estate in north London, built in the early 1900s.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a planned leafy residential district on a town's edge, of which the Hampstead estate is the best-known British example.

clue.text: Classified as "U" — felt in the dark about it

indicators.note: the groping goes about it, that is around the letter U just named, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to feel one's way blindly is to grope, past tense groped
the letter U is given as written, in quotes

explanation.surface: A film certified U for universal viewing, oddly linked to fumbling in a dark cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'U' is the British film certificate for all audiences, which suits the cinema picture; here it is just the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Things classified have been sorted into categories, which is what being grouped means.

clue.text: He who gets up to go down?

definitions.text: He who gets up to go down?

parts.words: He who gets up to go down?
parts.note: one who gets out of bed is a person rising; also the upright board of each stair, climbed to go up and walked over to go down

explanation.surface: A riddle about someone who rises only in order to descend.
explanation.walkthrough: The person who gets up is an early or late one in bed; the second sense is the vertical part of a stair step, which you pass going downstairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who leaves bed in the morning is so called, and the same word names the vertical part of each stair.

clue.text: As an example seniors may be going forth

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: the seniors may be rearranged into something else, so their letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Older people are offered as an instance of those likely to head out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' is the anagram signal; 'seniors' reads as older people heading out, but only its letters matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A going out or departure is the formal sense of the noun, from the same root as exit-door egress.

clue.text: Reputed to be heavy around one

indicators.note: the word for heavy goes around the numeral one, enclosing it

parts.note: heavy can mean dense and badly risen, like a sad cake or heavy-hearted
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is said to be weighty, give or take a single unit.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'sad' cake or loaf is one that has failed to rise, so heavy; the sense of gloom works too.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reputed is commonly claimed, as in 'he is said to be rich'.

clue.text: Amused by cunning devices in a plot

indicators.note: the crafty tricks sit in the plot of ground, one piece inside the other

parts.note: a plot of garden ground is a bed
guile is crafty trickery

explanation.surface: Schemers are entertained by the clever stratagems of a conspiracy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' reads as a conspiracy, matching 'cunning devices', but it is a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To beguile is to charm or divert, so a person beguiled has been entertained or charmed.

clue.text: Regret about drive being up due to mischief-maker

indicators.note: the regret goes about the turned drive, enclosing it

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: in a down clue, being up means the word drive is read from bottom to top

parts.note: go means energy or drive, as in get-up-and-go

explanation.surface: Sorrow because someone's ambition is spent, and all thanks to a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being up' turns the drive word backwards before it sits inside the regret; 'drive' means energy, not motoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal or scamp who causes trouble is a classic sense of the word, as in a lovable rascal.

clue.text: Caught unconscious about real trouble

indicators.note: the word for unconscious goes about the jumbled letters, enclosing them

parts.note: out cold means unconscious

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters of real are disturbed

explanation.surface: A victim knocked out cold over a genuine difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' jumbles the letters of real, which then split the word for unconscious after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Collaring someone is seizing them by the neck, so informally arresting or capturing them.

clue.text: Inclined to be guarded

definitions.meaning: had a tendency, as in 'he leaned towards'

explanation.surface: A person disposed to be cautious and protective.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the past tense of two verbs, one meaning to lean towards a habit, the other to look after.

clue.text: Following saying. .

definitions.meaning: obeying or keeping, as one keeps a rule or a festival

explanation.surface: Read with the next clue, it introduces an old maxim.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots join this clue to the next one, making one sentence; each half stands alone as a double definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means keeping rules or customs and also remarking, as in 'he said, observing the weather'.

clue.text: … is a maxim for a dwarf

definitions.meaning: a short pithy saying or aphorism
a small mythical earth-dwelling creature, guardian of treasure

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue, a proverb is said to be fit for a little man.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots continue clue 9, but this clue works alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an aphorism (from Greek gnome, a thought) and a small legendary underground being.

clue.text: Study intently for every purpose

parts.note: per means for each, as in miles per hour
a use is a purpose or function

explanation.surface: A student reads closely so that everything has some point.
explanation.definitionFit: To read through something carefully and thoroughly is the word's proper sense.

clue.text: Reigning beauty in a hat is unfairly satirised

indicators.note: the beauty is put in the hat, one piece inside the other

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
the belle of the ball is the reigning beauty

explanation.surface: The queen of beauty in a bonnet is mocked unjustly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lid' is informal for a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Being defamed with false published statements fits being mocked unjustly in print.

clue.text: Item set apart for special service

definitions.meaning: a single particular or small point
in military use, to assign soldiers to a particular task

explanation.surface: A single thing is reserved for a particular duty.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a particular point or small part; the military verb is to assign troops to a duty.

clue.text: Highest score? Fine

parts.note: top means highest
a notch is a scored cut or mark

explanation.surface: A question about the best result, answered with approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score' looks like points in a game; it is a cut mark, as notched on a tally stick.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate or excellent is the informal sense of the hyphenated adjective.

clue.text: Certainly in drink, but restrained

indicators.note: the word for certainly goes in the drink, one inside the other

parts.note: mead is a drink made from fermented honey
sure is an informal yes, certainly

explanation.surface: A drinker is definitely tipsy yet keeps self-control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in drink' suggests drunkenness, but it is the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful, deliberate manner is calm and controlled, as in a considered, unhurried response.

clue.text: Idiot — to get tight and then dance

parts.note: to screw something is to tighten it
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A fool getting drunk and then dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' suggests drunkenness; it is fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: An eccentric or crazy person is the American slang sense.

clue.text: Capacity to inspire followers in a march is unusual

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A leader's magnetism shows when a protest walk turns out unusually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the letters of A MARCH IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal magnetism that draws devotion is the word's sense, used of leaders.

clue.text: Born writer finishes with the drug

indicators.note: the run ends with the word the, so it is placed last

parts.note: NE comes from née, born, used for a maiden name
a pen is a writing instrument
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author ends his career drugged.
explanation.walkthrough: Nepenthe is the drug of forgetfulness in Homer's Odyssey.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend it was a potion that banished grief and memory, so any soothing narcotic.

clue.text: One Conservative in residence is very particular

indicators.note: the two letters are placed in the residence, one piece inside the other

parts.note: a nest is a home or residence
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the abbreviation for Conservative in British politics

explanation.surface: A Tory living at home is extremely fussy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its old sense means fastidious or precise, so the superlative means most fussy.

clue.text: Ground down by some Herod edict

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is crushed by an order of the biblical King Herod.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in hEROD EDict.
explanation.definitionFit: Worn away gradually, as rock is by water, is to be worn down.

clue.text: Edward comes up bothering 2 — he wants something

indicators.note: in a down clue, comes up means the short name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ed is short for Edward

indicators.note: bothering means disturbing, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: the number points to the answer of clue 2-down, one who gets up

explanation.surface: Edward rises to pester someone, wanting something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' turns ED to DE; 'bothering' rearranges the 2-down answer into SIRER.
explanation.definitionFit: One who longs for or craves something is the literal agent noun of to wish.

clue.text: Pots needed for cold part of the garden

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
a rockery is a garden area of stones and alpine plants

explanation.surface: Plant pots are wanted for a chilly corner of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pots' suggests flower pots in the garden; it means dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthenware plates, cups and dishes collectively are household pottery.

clue.text: Two kings — one makes money abroad

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
R is from Rex, Latin for king
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two monarchs, and one of them makes a fortune overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: The krone is the currency of Denmark and Norway.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Scandinavian currency unit, foreign money to a British solver.

clue.text: Laborious tasks for the wife in country mansions

indicators.note: the wife's letter goes in the mansions, one piece inside the other

parts.note: a seat is a large country house, as in a family seat
W is the abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: Hard chores are set for the wife in grand country houses.
explanation.walkthrough: A country seat is a British aristocratic family's estate house.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard toils that make one perspire are informally named after the perspiring itself.

clue.text: A good man about — he wins the plate

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the good man goes about the word he, enclosing it

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A virtuous man is around, and he takes the prize trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: An ashet is a large serving plate, a Scottish and northern English word from French assiette.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a regional word for a big oval serving dish.

clue.text: A divided populace in a Biblical land

indicators.note: the populace is divided by the letter A, which splits it open

parts.note: the mob is the common people, the populace

explanation.surface: A split nation living in a land from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: Moab was a kingdom east of the Dead Sea in the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Old Testament kingdom of Ruth's people, east of the Dead Sea.

clue.text: Secretary takes care of a painting on dry plaster

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: An office secretary looks after a mural.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the fresco technique of painting onto plaster that has already dried, Italian for dry.

clue.text: Match rose material for front of dress

indicators.note: the letters become material, made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pick a rose-coloured fabric to go on the bodice of a gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'material' reads as cloth but signals the rearrangement of MATCH ROSE.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an ornamental triangular panel filling the front of a bodice in older fashions.

clue.text: Carrier for a pusher

parts.note: a pusher sounds like a drug dealer, but here is a parent pushing a baby carriage

explanation.surface: A bag for a drug dealer's goods.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'pusher' suggests a drug dealer; the carrier is a baby carriage, which is pushed.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the full form of pram, a wheeled baby carriage that a parent pushes along.
